questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to Italy, and I wanted to be in a city big enough to explore and where there was easy access to get around and see more of Italy

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy as the erasmus office in Milano was very informative, and if I needed any information they were quick to answer my emails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received assistance from Massimo, and it was easy to find out when and where to find the office he was sitting at. I don't remember needing any more information than what was received

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Milano is very expensive, so it was hard to find something that was both affordable, but also nice to live in and have enough rooms to house me and my roommate. But if you don't have money as an issue there are a lot of appartements. I found my appartement at UniPlace which has been working out really well, with no scam, but still expensive with a lot of extra fees. To find good accomodation I will recommend looking a couple months before arrival, we found our appartement in early october and arrived in early january. I think even earlier would work out fine as well. I didn't see living on campus as an option as there are not a lot of spots and it's a bit out of the city.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's expensive, and make sure to research the nice neighborhoods with good public transport. Spend the extra money to live inside the city and not outside the city ring because you only live there for a short amount of time, and it's nice to walk around and live close to cafees and restaurants.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I remember it being difficult to find the courses available at my faculty and the level, but once i found out it was easy as the schedules were easy to find as well. But I still think the registration process is a bit weird, since it actually doesn't matter much before you arrive, as there are no deadline at La Statale, so you should only find some courses to add into your learning agreement, and then try different courses upon arrival

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I don't remember any help being available

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted, but I was dissapointed in the level, as it is way easier in Milano than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't have any advice per say

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It's lower than at UCPH, and the courses were not as expected as I believed that they would be harder and give me more knowledge than I already had. But some of them were interesting

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There are a lot more participation involved and some courses also have attendence. Some courses also include a presentation that you have to prepare, where the full grade depends on both that and the exam. In Italy the rules about exams and courses are more bendable than in UCPH. Fx we got an exam moved because the date didn't fit us. None of the exams I had were on computer, everything is mostly based on pen and paper.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
International Macroeconomics 12 ECTS
Global Challenges to Democracy 6 ECTS
Dirty Hands Politics: War, terrorism and torture 6 ECTS
Global Social Inequalities 9 ECTS

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Global Challenges to Democracy was the most interesting course and oragnized the best. The professor was great and the topic is really relevant in these times. International Macroeconomics was fine, but it was mostly a repetition of what I was taught before, which was dissapointing. 
As the level and difficulty at the university isn't that high I would recommend taking some classes that sounds interestering instead of academically challenging, and maybe choose a topic you already know something about, if you want to chill a bit.

Food DKK per month *

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
I didn't get my metrocard early on, so I used too many money on just paying for each trip I took. My unexpected costs is mostly just me going out and taking a lot of trips, which I don't count for unexpected, but I used a lot of money to just explore and have fun. I don't remember having any "serious" unexpected costs.
My 6000 food costs include everything i consumed which is also apperativo, drinks, eating out etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out can be really cheap where you can eat primi and dessert and drink wine for only 150-200 kr. Public transport in all of italy is really cheap, we only paid 600 kr. out and home from Milano to Napoli with high speed train, which i think is really cheap. Busses are also easy to get around with.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't believe in looking for any as i found my social activities with other exchange students from Denmark. Erasmusprogram didn't work for me, as I arrived early january and it didn't start until late february.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sports, clubs, apperativo

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to San Siro atleast once, it's a huge stadium and you can get cheap tickets. Go to as many cities on daytrips as you can and don't stress about planning way too much ahead as most of the trips are spontanious and can be planned in five minutes as the transport are easy and accessable. Go clubbing, it's really fun!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, because I knew a lot about Italy beforehand and once you go around the city and explore and go out, it's really easy to adapt to the culture and the way of living

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I mostly socialized with people from Denmark, but the few italians I spoke to, were the once i had class with. They were very friendly and wanted to help out and drink apperativo. But just be really open and talk to people and ask what they study and where they are from, people are usually open to erasmus students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Language. If they don't speak english, they just speak italian to you, which can be difficult sometimes. Our landlord didn't speak english so that was a bit difficult. I don't think Milano is the most difficult city to be in as a foreigner as it is a very international city

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food culture, the relaxed way of living and taking things more as they come. La Dolce Vita is really no joke

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Go for the experience, not the academics 
Relax and don't stress about doing something all the time, a lot about being on exchange is the daily life and getting to know the city, you will have a lot of freetime, but enjoy it because back home you will have all your responsibilites again
Don't worry too much about money and try to say yes to as many things you can

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Choose interesting courses, do what you can't do at home such as eat out, read a book etc.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To have so much freetime, and meeting a lot of new people as everyone is open to have fun and go out. It was nice to just be able to go for a run and having nothing else to do that day. I really enjoyed seeing so much of Italy!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To live in the moment and worrying if I got the most out of it

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
